title: Police shoot driver dead after chase
subtitle: Father of two dies in a hail of bullets on Commissioners St. when police try to stop a compact car that had sped away from other officers following a brief chase early Monday.
article: A Mississauga father of two, who was shot to death by police in Toronto's Port Lands area early Monday, was coping with a mental illness and struggling to get his family life in order, according to people who knew him.

Wieslaw Duda died in a hail of bullets on Commissioners St. near Cherry St. when police tried to stop a compact car that had sped away from other officers following a brief chase at 1 a.m. Monday. The Special Investigations Unit, the provincial police watchdog, is investigating because the victim was shot to death during a confrontation with police.
"This is just horrible. He was harmless and very friendly to everybody," Magdalena Mazurek, who lives in the same Lakeshore Rd. E. building Duda had moved into with his teenage son about a year ago.
Mazurek occasionally ran into Duda when she walked her dog. She described him as a cordial man.
"His son told me his father was schizophrenic, but I've always known him to be a nice person. His son loves him. It's terrible for him," she said.

On Linby St., in the Cawthra Rd. and The Queensway area where Duda's mother, sister and brother-in-law live, the police shooting came as a surprise to many of the Polish neighbours who have known the family for years.
"It's such a shock. I can't even think straight," said a next-door neighbour who has known the family for more than a decade.

The neighbour, who did not want to be identified, said Duda, 50, his parents, wife and son, about 18, and two sisters immigrated to Canada from Poland about 14 years ago. He has also has a daughter about 7 years old.
Duda who had worked in a Mississauga factory was separated from his wife and had recently gone on a medical disability leave, according to the neighbour.
"He was so proud of his daughter. When you saw them together, you could tell how happy they were," she said.

He and his wife lived in separate apartments and shared custody of their daughter who would occasionally stay at her grandmother's house, as did her older brother. Duda's father died several years ago, the neighbour said.
"Everybody will tell you, he seemed like a nice gentleman. He wouldn't walk by without saying hello."
Although Duda and his wife lived apart for more than a year, they still had contact with each other through their children.
"They spoke to each other and were planning to get together - to become a family again. This is so sad," the neighbour added.
According to the SIU, police began pursuing a car at Leslie St. and Commissioners St. at 1 a.m. Monday.

Soon after, police stopped following the car, but later located it at Cherry and Commissioners Sts. At that intersection, one officer was struck by the car and the driver of the silver Nissan Sentra was fatally shot.
The officer was taken to St. Michael's Hospital with minor injuries and released later in the day.

Police cordoned off the scene Monday morning, and Cherry St. remained closed south of Lake Shore Blvd. E. while the SIU continued to investigate along with forensic officers and the collision reconstruction unit.

At the intersection, the Nissan remained blocked by five police cruisers, and another three police cruisers were parked behind it. The Nissan's front doors were open, its body dented, and several of its windows shattered. A dozen bullet holes had punctured the right side of the vehicle and its front window, and a few shotgun shells littered the ground behind the car. A nearby police cruiser had a flat tire.
The car appeared to have been making a right turn onto Cherry St. when it was stopped.
The SIU investigates all cases of serious injury, death and sexual assault involving the police.
Anyone who may have information about the incident is asked to contact the SIU at 416-622-0748 or 1-800-787-8529.
